name: Anders Westermann
current_role: Co-owner (Westermann family) of WS Audiology via T&W Medical; former Executive Vice President of Widex
profile: Son of Widex co-founder Erik Westermann; with brother Søren and cousin Jan Tøpholm he ran Danish hearing-aid maker Widex as Executive VP. The Tøpholm and Westermann families merged Widex with Sivantos in 2019 to form WS Audiology, which they co-own with EQT via T&W Medical.
interesting_fact: Widex was founded in 1956 by Christian Tøpholm and Erik Westermann; their sons (Jan Tøpholm, Anders and Søren Westermann) later ran the company together as second-generation leaders.
notes: Very private; little recent public info. Identity of the Hurun-listed person inferred from family ownership; MarketScreener 'Anders Steen Westermann' (Widex director since 1980) may be the same person but unconfirmed. Best route likely via WS Audiology corporate communications.

name: Yen Chen Lilian
current_role: Chairwoman and Group CEO, Yulon Group (Yulon Motor), Taiwan
profile: Lilian Chen Yen (嚴陳莉蓮) is the widow of Yulon chairman Kenneth Yen (嚴凱泰), and took over leadership of Taiwan's Yulon automotive group after his death in 2018. She now steers its Nissan/Mitsubishi partnerships, EV contract manufacturing with Foxtron (Hon Hai), North American energy storage and the Yulon City mall in Xindian.
interesting_fact: In Dec 2025 Yulon sold its home-grown Luxgen brand to Foxtron (Hon Hai's EV JV) for NT$787.6m while keeping a ~43.8% stake in Foxtron.
deep_cut_fact: Before business she was a Taiwan women's national basketball player and captain of the Tai Yuen women's team; an alumna of Chinese Culture University's PE dept, she gave NT$10m in 2025 to fund scholarships and the men's basketball team there.
notes: Taiwanese, not mainland (Hurun lists 'China'). Email is Yulon Motor's spokesperson/company contact from exchange filings (spokesperson Cho Che-yu); verify on MOPS. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Clemens Toennies
current_role: Managing partner (Geschäftsführender Gesellschafter), Premium Food Group (formerly Tönnies Holding), Rheda-Wiedenbrück
profile: Trained butcher who co-founded Tönnies with brother Bernd in 1971 and built it into Germany's largest meat processor; he owns about 45%. Rebranded in 2025 as Premium Food Group (~€8bn revenue, ~22,000 staff) to diversify beyond meat, with son Max increasingly taking over management. He turned 70 in May 2026.
interesting_fact: Chaired the supervisory board of football club FC Schalke 04 from 2001 to 2020; the company HQ in Rheda-Wiedenbrück even has its own football pitch with heated turf.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he wanted to become a radio and TV mechanic rather than a butcher; he was just 15 when the company was registered with his brother and needed his parents' signature. His parents' shop processed only seven pigs a week.
notes: Press email is head of corporate communications as published in a June 2020 press release; may be outdated post-2025 rebrand. Avoid Schalke 2019-20 controversy topics. Born 27 May 1956, fifth of six children.

name: Simone Maag de Moura Cunha
current_role: Shareholder (~3.5%) of Straumann Group; no public executive role found
profile: Per Forbes, she owns about 3.5% of Swiss dental-implant maker Straumann Group. She is the niece of billionaire Rudolf Maag (Straumann's second-largest shareholder, who built Stratec Medical and merged it with Synthes) and sister-in-law of Straumann chairman-family member Thomas Straumann.
interesting_fact: Her uncle Rudolf Maag bought Straumann's medical device division in 1990, took it public as Stratec Medical, then merged it with Synthes in 1999; that stake was later sold to Johnson & Johnson.
notes: Extremely private; no independent public profile, interviews or verified accounts found. Only route is via Straumann Group corporate communications, and she has no operating role there. Low priority.

name: Andrew Brode
current_role: Non-Executive Director, RWS Holdings plc (interim Chair Jan–Oct 2026, succeeded by Patrick De Smedt)
profile: Chartered accountant who sold a family publishing business to Wolters Kluwer, bought legal journal Eclipse in 1990, and merged it with translation firm RWS in 1995, building RWS into a global AI-driven language and IP services group via acquisitions. Long-time RWS chairman and major shareholder; also a key backer/chair of Learning Technologies Group.
interesting_fact: Took over as interim chair of RWS when the chair left at end-2025, then handed over to ex-Microsoft EMEA chairman Patrick De Smedt in Oct 2026 while staying on the board.
deep_cut_fact: An Old Edwardian (left 1959), he funded half of King Edward's School Birmingham's £5m 2012 appeal and much of the school's new sports hall, named The Andrew Brode Sports Centre.
notes: Passionate mentor of young entrepreneurs (coached LTG's Jonathan Satchell, Cera's Mahiben Maruthappu) — good angle for an entrepreneurship podcast. Route via RWS company secretary or MHP.
